note: Triennial election of Coleraine rural district (21 divisions, one member each). Nominations were received on 21 April 1927; there was no contest in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12). Eighteen members were returned unopposed. No nomination was received for Articlave (previous member James Millen), Bovagh (H. Y. Henderson) or Drumcroon (James Mairs); the previous members continued in office, as the Northern Whig's list (30 April 1927, p. 9) prints, and are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Polled Friday 27 May 1927: 'Polling took place yesterday in the Bellarena division of county Londonderry, the only division in the county where there was a contest' for the county council (Londonderry Sentinel, Saturday 28 May 1927, p. 8), and the Limavady rural contest in Straw 'took place on Friday' (Derry Journal, 30 May 1927, p. 8). No nomination; the previous member, Jas. Millen, continued in office (deemed re-elected). Division from the nominations report itself ('Articlave - No nomination (previous member, Jas. Millen)'). At the Guardians' meeting of 28 May 1927 he announced his intention of retiring from public life (Ballymoney Free Press, 2 June 1927, p. 3), but he sat at the annual meeting of the new council on 1 June 1927 and was re-appointed one of its representatives on the County Committee of Agriculture; he left the council in 1928 and was co-opted an urban guardian for Coleraine in June 1928 (Ballymoney Free Press, 28 June 1928, p. 4). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
